status_vocabulary.supported: the operation is implemented against the real provider API, exercised by tests today, and meets the tracker-contract.md #4.2 target guarantee for its journey family
status_vocabulary.gap: the operation is required by a core journey (operations[].core == true) but is unimplemented, explicitly refused by the adapter, or below the #4.2 target guarantee; blocks V1 exit for that provider until the owner ticket closes it. A non-core operation is never a gap: an unimplemented non-core capability is 'refused' instead
status_vocabulary.refused: the adapter's refusal is deliberate and never blocks V1 exit. Valid ONLY on a non-core operation (operations[].core == false): criterion 1 requires every core operation to reach 'supported', so an unsupported core operation is always 'gap' or 'to_qualify', both of which block V1 exit for that provider
status_vocabulary.to_qualify: the operation's real behaviour against the live provider is not qualified; PAT-65 must qualify it on authorized test resources before any other status can be asserted. On a core operation, 'to_qualify' blocks V1 exit for that provider exactly like 'gap'; only the reason differs (unqualified transport vs. known-missing implementation). On a non-core operation 'to_qualify' is temporary: before V1 exit it must resolve to 'supported' or to 'refused' with a typed refusal (never a bare NotImplementedError), and it names its owner ticket (PAT-65 unless stated)

cell_fields.ticket: owner ticket (PAT-<n>); required on every core 'gap' and 'to_qualify' cell and on every non-core 'to_qualify' cell
cell_fields.blocked_by_adr: id of an entry in pending_adrs; present when closing the cell changes a durable invariant, so no code may land before that ADR is explicitly accepted

open_points_not_decided_here.description: GitHub Projects v2 is GraphQL-only. Foundry's code-host rule is 'Never GraphQL ... REST only — the adapter enforces it' (skills/merge-pr/SKILL.md:226). A repository choosing ghprojects keeps the REST-only GitHub code-host adapter for PRs/merges, but its tracker adapter would need GraphQL. PAT-65 resolves this tension; PAT-53 does not.
